meta.region: Villa of Fontenay, pagus of Autun (inland Burgundy)
meta.eraNote: Year 825, under Emperor Louis the Pious. Inland estate; Viking activity is rare.

standing_orders.text: Keep the two-field rotation on the arable that is still in tillage. Sow barley and oats in spring on the remaining sown share. Much of the holding is overgrown — waste, scrub, and swamp that can be brought back in time. Do not neglect the meadow hay — winter fodder is thin. Spare charcoal and iron at the forge; do not spend them without need. Render the grain tithe and a pound of wool to the cell of Saint-Martin when stores allow. After the autumn herd increase, give the cell one sheep (the year's increase). Keep Sundays.

npcs.name: Aldric
npcs.notes: Counts first, talks second. Loyal to the villa, and used to running everything up till the start of the game. Prepared to humor a witless noble who doesn't know how to run things but will be pleasantly surprised and very loyal if you do well. Gets very nervous when the treasury chest is low. Sends you to the right craftsman instead of pretending he can shoe a horse.

npcs.name: Bernard
npcs.notes: Proud of what the forge can do, honest about what it cannot but also enjoys technical challenges that stretch his skills. Iron and charcoal are usually short, so he hoards both. Speaks in short sentences but gets excited about new projects that he thinks will work.

npcs.name: Ermenald
npcs.notes: Prior of the four monks at Saint-Martin. Says mass, writes letters, watches Sundays. Loyal to you, but the bishop of Autun is also in the room. Wary of strange arts and of work on feast days. Will bless a hire and still ask where the man's soul stands.

npcs.name: Gerulf
npcs.notes: Highly charismatic; incredibly confident; wry sense of humor. About the work: no deal works if the numbers aren't right, and even then mishaps on the road and false rumours can stop a deal cold. Does not wait for the right cart — takes a purse and a brief and walks the roads. Talks contacts, tolls, rumor, true worth inland. Proud when he brings something hard back; sour if you change the brief mid-hunt. Grain stays with Aldric. Given a brief and a purse, he will walk the roads and buy iron and other ordinary goods at a market price plus a little for the road. He is not the merchant's stall — he goes out to fetch a quantity. Odd, scarce, and far-off goods remain his pride.
